mainTopic: שבועת ביטוי: future vs. past oaths, and which kinds of forgetting bring a קרבן
overview: The amud opens by noting that one of the earlier statements was really said by רב פפא. It then asks whether a שבועת ביטוי covers only oaths about the future, as רבי ישמעאל says, or also oaths about the past, as רבי עקיבא says. רבי יוחנן explains that they read the פסוק (ויקרא 5:4) with different methods learned from their teachers. רבי עקיבא uses ריבה ומיעט, so almost everything is included except a דבר מצוה. רבי ישמעאל uses כלל ופרט וכלל, so only future oaths count. רבי יצחק and רב יצחק בר אבין each explain why the 'future' feature of the detail is the one that matters. A ברייתא then teaches that the קרבן is not brought by an אונס, shown by the story of רב כהנא and רב אסי. Nor is it brought by a מזיד, or by someone who forgot only the item rather than the oath. The rest of the amud asks whether forgetting the item without forgetting the oath can even happen. רב יוסף and אביי debate the bread-basket case. רב אשי's reminder test for someone who forgot both is rejected by רבינא, and the גמרא concludes that there is no difference. A new question from רבא to רב נחמן begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Correcting who said one of the earlier statements
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that one of the earlier statements was said by רב פפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of those statements was said by רב פפא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the previous discussion with a small correction about who said what. One of the statements just quoted actually belongs to רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing in the law changes here. The גמרא is only fixing the attribution, so that one of the two earlier statements is credited to רב פפא and not to the person it was first credited to.

phrases.english: One of them (those statements)
Rav Pappa said it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the previous sugya, which comes before this section, with a note about attribution.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One of the previous statements is credited to רב פפא.

steps.title: Quoting רבי ישמעאל from the משנה: only future oaths
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's view of רבי ישמעאל that liability applies only to oaths about the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: One is liable only for an oath about the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. It is setting up a discussion of where רבי ישמעאל's view comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי ישמעאל, a שבועת ביטוי makes someone liable for a קרבן only when he swears about something he will or won't do. An oath about something that already happened would not be included.

keyTerms.meaning: The future, what is still to come
An oath spoken about doing or not doing something

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא עַל הֶעָתִיד לָבֹא.
phrases.english: He is liable only for (an oath about) the future.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא עַל הֶעָתִיד לָבֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי ישמעאל, a שבועת ביטוי makes one liable only when it is about the future.

steps.title: The ברייתא asks about matters with no harm or good
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא notes that the פסוק mentions 'harm or good' and asks where we learn that other matters are included.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'To do harm or to do good.' From this I only know about matters that involve harm and good. From where do we know about matters that do not involve harm and good?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that reads the פסוק closely. It asks a question that the next step will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'to do harm or to do good' seem to limit the oath to things that hurt or help a person. The ברייתא wants to know which words in the פסוק widen the law to cover other matters as well.

keyTerms.meaning: To do harm or to do good

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"To do harm or to do good"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:4

phrases.english: I only know (about) matters
that involve harm and good;
(matters) that do not involve harm and good, from where (do we know)?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לְהָרַע אוֹ לְהֵיטִיב אֵין לִי אֶלָּא דְּבָרִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶן הֲרָעָה וַהֲטָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that explains the sources behind the dispute in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which words in the פסוק include matters that involve no harm or good?

steps.title: The opening words of the פסוק include all matters
steps.stepSummary: The words 'or if a person swears, expressing with his lips' include matters with no harm or good.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Or if a person swears, expressing with his lips.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question by pointing to the opening words of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The broad phrase 'a person swears, expressing with his lips' is read as including any oath, even one about matters that involve no harm or good. So the law is not limited by the words 'harm or good.'

phrases.english: The verse says:
"Or if a person swears,
expressing with his lips."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:4

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: אוֹ נֶפֶשׁ כִּי תִשָּׁבַע לְבַטֵּא בִשְׂפָתַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'or if a person swears, expressing with his lips' include matters that involve no harm or good.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא includes oaths about the past
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns oaths about the past from 'whatever a person expresses in an oath,' according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know about the future. From where do we know about the past? The פסוק says: 'Whatever a person expresses in an oath.' These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks and answers a second question: where do we learn that oaths about the past also count? It tells us this is the view of רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain wording points to future actions. רבי עקיבא uses the next widening phrase of the פסוק, 'whatever a person expresses,' to include oaths about what already happened. So רבי עקיבא uses one phrase for matters with no harm or good, and a second phrase for the past.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source behind the view that a person can be liable for a false oath about something that already happened.

phrases.english: I only know (about oaths) about the future,
about the past, from where (do we know)?
The verse says:
"Whatever a person expresses in an oath."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:4

phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא לְהַבָּא, לְשֶׁעָבַר מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second inclusion: oaths about the past.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, oaths about the past are included, learned from 'whatever a person expresses in an oath.'

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: 'harm or good' means only the future
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל reads 'to do harm or to do good' as limiting the oath to the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: 'To do harm or to do good' means the future.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל gives his source for the view in the משנה. He disagrees with רבי עקיבא about oaths concerning the past.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can only do harm or do good in the future. So רבי ישמעאל understands the פסוק as speaking only about oaths for the future, and he does not include oaths about the past.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says:
"To do harm or to do good" (means) the future.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: לְהָרַע אוֹ לְהֵיטִיב לְהַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי עקיבא's inclusion of the past.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words 'to do harm or to do good' limit שבועת ביטוי to the future.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא challenges: how do you include matters with no harm or good?
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא asks רבי ישמעאל how his reading can include matters that involve no harm or good.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: If so, I only know about matters that involve good and harm. From where do we know about matters that do not involve harm and good?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא challenges רבי ישמעאל's reading of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'harm or good' is a real limit, it should also exclude matters that involve no harm or good. But רבי ישמעאל also wants to include those matters. So רבי עקיבא asks what source he has for including them.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: אִם כֵּן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him: If so,
I only know (about) matters
that involve good and harm,
matters that do not involve
harm and good, from where (do we know)?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: אִם כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי ישמעאל's reading in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's use of 'to do harm or to do good' as a limit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If those words limit the law, they should also exclude matters with no harm or good. So what source includes those matters?

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: from the widening of the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל answers that matters with no harm or good are included by the widening language of the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: From the widening of the פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל answers רבי עקיבא's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל admits that the פסוק has broad, including language. He uses that broad language to add matters with no harm or good, but he still keeps the limit to the future.

keyTerms.meaning: A widening (inclusion) in the פסוק's wording

phrases.english: He said to him:
From the widening of the verse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to an inclusive word in the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ישמעאל seemed to have no source for matters with no harm or good.
steps.terutzMaskana: Those matters come from the widening language of the פסוק.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the same widening includes the past
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא argues that if the פסוק widens to include one thing, it widens to include the past as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If the פסוק widened for this, the פסוק widened for that!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא turns רבי ישמעאל's answer back against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once you agree the פסוק widens beyond 'harm or good,' those words are no longer a strict limit. So the same widening should also include oaths about the past.
steps.confusionAlert: The two 'לכך' mean different things. The first 'this' is matters with no harm or good; the second 'that' is oaths about the past.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא includes both matters with no harm or good and oaths about the past. רבי ישמעאל includes matters with no harm or good but limits the oath to the future. רבי עקיבא argues that once the פסוק widens at all, it widens for the past too.

phrases.english: He said to him:
If the verse widened for this,
the verse widened for that!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם רִיבָּה הַכָּתוּב לְכָךְ, רִיבָּה הַכָּתוּב לְכָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי ישמעאל's answer in step 8 and turns it against him.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's choice to widen the פסוק for one thing but not for the past.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A widening that breaks the 'harm or good' limit for one case should also break the limit to the future.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's argument seems correct
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי עקיבא's point against רבי ישמעאל sounds right, so why doesn't רבי ישמעאל accept it?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא made a good point to רבי ישמעאל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reacts to the argument from Step 9 and says it sounds convincing. This sets up the question: why would רבי ישמעאל still disagree?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 9, רבי עקיבא argued that if the widening words of the פסוק can include one thing, they can include oaths about the past too. The גמרא agrees this sounds strong. That makes רבי ישמעאל's position hard to understand, and an explanation is needed.

phrases.english: He said it well to him,
Rabbi Akiva to Rabbi Yishmael!
phrases.notes: The unspoken question is: so why doesn't רבי ישמעאל agree?

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁפִּיר קָא אָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא backs רבי עקיבא's argument from Step 9 and asks why רבי ישמעאל rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's limiting of oaths to the future
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא's argument seems logically strong, so רבי ישמעאל's refusal to include the past seems unjustified.

steps.title: Each sage follows his teacher's method of reading
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that רבי ישמעאל reads the תורה with כלל ופרט, as his teacher did, and רבי עקיבא reads it with ריבה ומיעט, as his teacher did.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: רבי ישמעאל served רבי נחוניא בן הקנה, who read the whole תורה using 'general and detail,' so he also reads that way. רבי עקיבא served נחום איש גם זו, who read the whole תורה using 'widening and narrowing,' so he also reads that way.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers why the two sages disagree. Each one uses a different method of reading פסוקים, learned from his own teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is not really about logic. It is about which reading method to use. With כלל ופרט, the detail sets the limit, so 'to do harm or to do good' narrows oaths to the future. With ריבה ומיעט, the widening words win, and only a small thing is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Served, meaning he was a student of that teacher
General and detail: a method where the detail limits the general statement
Widening and narrowing: a method where the widening words include almost everything
Interprets, learns out from a פסוק

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains many arguments between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא across ש״ס. They often disagree because they use different reading methods.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי ישמעאל ignores the widening words. He also uses them, as in Step 8, but under his method the detail sets the limits.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל – שֶׁשִּׁימֵּשׁ אֶת רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, who served Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKana,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה דּוֹרֵשׁ אֶת כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ
phrases.english: who would interpret the entire Torah
with general and detail,
he too interprets with general and detail.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא – שֶׁשִּׁימֵּשׁ אֶת נַחוּם אִישׁ גַּם זוֹ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva, who served Nachum of Gam Zo,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה דּוֹרֵשׁ אֶת כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ
phrases.english: who would interpret the entire Torah
with widening and narrowing,
he too interprets with widening and narrowing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל שֶׁשִּׁימֵּשׁ אֶת רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10 by tracing the dispute to two different methods of reading the תורה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different methods of reading the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ישמעאל seemed to have no good answer to רבי עקיבא's logic.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי ישמעאל uses כלל ופרט, so the detail limits the oath to the future. רבי עקיבא uses ריבה ומיעט, so the widening words include the past.

steps.title: Where does רבי עקיבא use widening and narrowing here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we see רבי עקיבא applying ריבויי ומיעוטי in this topic.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we see that רבי עקיבא interprets using widenings and narrowings?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source that shows רבי עקיבא's method at work in the פסוק of oaths. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן described רבי עקיבא's method in general terms. Now the גמרא wants to see exactly how it applies to the oath פסוק.

phrases.english: What is it that Rabbi Akiva
interprets with widenings and narrowings?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דְּדָרֵישׁ רִיבּוּיֵי וּמִיעוּטֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a concrete example of the method רבי יוחנן attributed to רבי עקיבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי עקיבא applies ריבה ומיעט to the oath פסוק.

steps.title: The verse widens, narrows, and widens again
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the oath פסוק as widening, narrowing, and widening again. Under this pattern, everything is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: 'Or if a person swears' widens. 'To do harm or to do good' narrows. 'Whatever a person expresses' widens again. When a פסוק widens, narrows, and widens again, it includes everything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that splits the פסוק into three parts: widening, narrowing, and widening again. The result is that almost every kind of oath is included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי עקיבא's method, the narrowing words in the middle do not set the limit. They only leave out one small thing. That is why oaths about the past are included too.

keyTerms.meaning: It went back and widened again

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
'Or if a person swears': it widened,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:4

phrases.english: 'to do harm or to do good': it narrowed,
'whatever a person expresses': it widened again;
widened, narrowed, and widened:
it included everything.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא אוֹ נֶפֶשׁ כִּי תִשָּׁבַע רִיבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12 with a ברייתא that shows the widen-narrow-widen pattern.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The oath פסוק follows the pattern ריבה ומיעט וריבה, which includes everything.

steps.title: What is included and what is left out
steps.stepSummary: The widening includes every kind of matter. The narrowing leaves out only a דבר מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did it include? It included all matters. And what did it leave out? It left out a דבר מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly what the widening includes and what the narrowing leaves out. Everything is included except a matter of מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under ריבה ומיעט וריבה, the narrowing words remove only one thing, a דבר מצוה. Everything else is included, even oaths about the past. That is the result רבי עקיבא argued for.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל (כלל ופרט): the detail limits oaths to the future. רבי עקיבא (ריבה ומיעט וריבה): everything is included, even the past, except a דבר מצוה.

phrases.english: What did it include?
It included all matters,
and what did it leave out?
It left out a matter of מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out what the widening and the narrowing in the ברייתא actually refer to.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The widening includes all matters. The narrowing excludes only a דבר מצוה.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל reads the oath פסוק as general, specific, general
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל splits the פסוק into כלל, פרט, and כלל again. So only things like the detail are included, and the detail is about the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל reads the פסוק as a general statement followed by a specific one. "Or if a person swears, expressing with his lips" is general. "To do bad or to do good" is specific. "Whatever a person may express" goes back to being general. With a general, a specific, and another general, you only include things that are like the specific. The specific case is clearly about the future, so everything included must be about the future.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא shows how רבי ישמעאל reads the same פסוק that רבי עקיבא read with ריבה ומיעט. He uses the rule of כלל ופרט וכלל instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The detail "להרע או להיטיב" describes oaths about something a person will do. Under כלל ופרט וכלל, only cases like the detail count. So רבי ישמעאל only makes a person liable for oaths about the future (להבא), not about the past (לשעבר).

keyTerms.meaning: A general term, then a specific one, then a general one again. This includes only things similar to the specific.
It went back and spoke generally again

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael interprets with general and specific:

phrases.aramaic: ״אוֹ נֶפֶשׁ כִּי תִשָּׁבַע לְבַטֵּא בִשְׂפָתַיִם״ – כְּלָל,
phrases.english: "Or if a person swears, expressing with his lips" is a general statement,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:4

phrases.english: "to do bad or to do good" is a specific detail,
"whatever a person may express": it went back and generalized;
general, specific, and general:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה דָן אֶלָּא כְעֵין הַפְּרָט;
phrases.english: you may only include things similar to the specific detail;
just as the detail is clearly about the future,
so too, everything included must be about the future.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבי ישמעאל's reading of the פסוק, to set beside רבי עקיבא's ריבה ומיעט reading in steps 13-14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under כלל ופרט וכלל, a שבועת ביטוי makes one liable only when it is about the future, like the detail "להרע או להיטיב".

steps.title: What the general words add and what the specific words remove
steps.stepSummary: The general words add future oaths even when they are not about doing bad or good. The specific words remove past oaths even when they are about doing bad or good.
steps.simpleTranslation: The general term does something: it brings in even matters that are not about doing bad or good, as long as they are about the future. The specific term also does something: it leaves out even matters that are about doing bad or good, if they are about the past.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly what each part of the פסוק accomplishes in רבי ישמעאל's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general words widen the rule past just "bad or good" oaths, so any future oath counts. The specific words narrow it to future oaths only. Each part has its own job, so neither is wasted.

keyTerms.meaning: It was useful for, it accomplished

phrases.english: The general term accomplished something:
to include even matters
that do not involve doing bad or good, about the future;
the specific term accomplished something:
to exclude even matters
that do involve doing bad or good, about the past.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains in detail what the כלל and the פרט of step 15 each add or remove.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Future oaths count even if they are not about bad or good. Past oaths do not count even if they are about bad or good.

steps.title: Why not flip what the general and specific words do?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we can't reverse it: the general words would include past oaths, and the specific words would exclude oaths that are not about bad or good.
steps.simpleTranslation: I can reverse it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading from step 16. Maybe the general and specific words should do each other's jobs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two features could make an oath "like the detail": being about the future, or being about bad or good. Why choose "future" as the feature that matters? One could instead say any bad-or-good oath counts, even about the past, while oaths that are not about bad or good are left out.

phrases.english: I will reverse it!
phrases.notes: Meaning: let the general words include past oaths, and let the specific words exclude oaths that are not about bad or good.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the way step 16 assigned jobs to the כלל and the פרט.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 16 that the detail limits oaths to the future rather than to matters of bad or good.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The detail has two features, future and bad-or-good. Nothing yet explains why "future" is the one that defines the category.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: the detail points to oaths that can be broken
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says oaths like "to do bad or good" are forbidden because of בל יחל דברו. A past oath is forbidden because of בל תשקרו instead, so it is left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: it must be similar to "to do bad or to do good." That means an oath whose prohibition comes from "he shall not break his word." This one is left out, since its prohibition does not come from "he shall not break his word." It comes from "you shall not lie."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers the challenge. He explains why "future" is the feature that truly matters in the detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A future oath, like the detail, becomes a sin only when the person breaks it later, which is בל יחל דברו. A false oath about the past is a lie the moment it is said, which is a different sin, בל תשקרו. So past oaths are a different kind of case and are not like the detail, and we cannot flip the reading.

keyTerms.meaning: "He shall not break his word": the ban on breaking a promise or oath

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי ישמעאל, a שבועת ביטוי is only about the future, because the detail in the פסוק describes an oath that can be broken (בל יחל דברו). A false oath about the past is a lie (בל תשקרו), which is a different kind of sin.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the basic difference between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא over whether a false oath about the past brings a קרבן עולה ויורד.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Similar to "to do bad or to do good":
an oath whose prohibition is because of "he shall not break his word";
phrases.notes: במדבר 30:3

phrases.english: this one is left out,
phrases.notes: "This one" means an oath about the past.

phrases.english: since its prohibition is not because of "he shall not break his word,"
but because of "you shall not lie."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:11

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: דּוּמְיָא דִּ״לְהָרַע אוֹ לְהֵיטִיב״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the איפוך אנא challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the defining feature of the detail: oaths whose sin is breaking one's word.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either feature of the detail (future, or bad-or-good) could define the category, so the reading could be flipped.
steps.terutzMaskana: The detail is defined by בל יחל דברו, which fits only future oaths. Past oaths fall under בל תשקרו and are excluded.

steps.title: The oath must come before the action
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר אבין gives another reason past oaths are left out: the פסוק speaks of an oath that comes first, followed by the action. In 'I ate' or 'I did not eat,' the action already happened before the oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר אבין said: The פסוק says 'Or if a person swears to utter with the lips.' This means the oath comes before the action, and not that the action comes before the oath. That leaves out 'I ate' and 'I did not eat,' where the action came before the oath.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק בר אבין gives a different answer to the question of step 17. He shows from the order of words in the פסוק that past oaths are left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק first says 'swears' and then 'to utter,' which he reads as the action. So the oath must come first and the action after it, which only happens with future oaths. In a past oath like 'I ate,' the eating already happened, so it cannot be included.

keyTerms.meaning: Uttering; here it means the action the oath is about
I ate (an oath about the past)

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer settles from the פסוק itself why the reversed reading in step 17 does not work: past oaths can never fit the פסוק.

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Avin said:
The verse says:
"Or if a person swears
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:4

phrases.english: to utter with the lips"
one whose oath comes before the uttering,
phrases.notes: Here 'uttering' means the action the oath talks about, like eating or not eating.

phrases.english: and not where the uttering comes before the oath;
this leaves out "I ate" and "I did not eat,"
where the action comes before the oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אָבִין אָמַר, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the question of step 17, alongside רבי יצחק's answer in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the order of words in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The general words might include past oaths.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק needs the oath to come before the action, so past oaths are left out.

steps.title: A ברייתא: forced and on-purpose cases are left out
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the פסוק that someone who broke his oath because he was forced, or who broke it on purpose, does not bring the קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'A man with an oath' leaves out someone who was forced. 'And it is hidden' leaves out someone who did it on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא about who must bring a קרבן for breaking a שבועת ביטוי. It learns two exemptions from words in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'A man with an oath' teaches that he is exempt if he was forced by things beyond his control. 'And it is hidden' shows the קרבן is only for someone who forgot, not for someone who broke the oath knowingly.
steps.confusionAlert: The מזיד is not let off easy. He broke the oath on purpose, so a קרבן does not help him at all.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"A man with an oath"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:4

phrases.english: leaves out someone who was forced.
"And it is hidden"
leaves out someone who did it on purpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic: who is exempt from the קרבן for breaking a שבועת ביטוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who was forced, or who broke the oath on purpose, does not bring the קרבן.

steps.title: He must forget the oath, not the object
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the קרבן is only for someone who forgot the oath itself. Someone who remembered the oath but forgot which item it was about is not liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'From him' means the oath was hidden from him. One might think he is liable even if he forgot the object. So the פסוק says 'with an oath, and it is hidden.' He is liable for forgetting the oath, but not for forgetting the object.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא learns from the word 'from him' that the קרבן is for forgetting the oath. It then rules out the case where he only forgot about the object.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first asks if forgetting the object might also count. It answers no, because the words 'with an oath, and it is hidden' are written side by side. That shows the oath itself must be what was hidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The object or item of the oath

steps.whatToRemember: The קרבן for שבועת ביטוי is only for someone who forgot the oath. Not for someone forced, not for someone who acted on purpose, and not for someone who only forgot the object.

phrases.english: "From him"
means that the oath was hidden from him.
One might think, even if the object was hidden from him?
phrases.notes: He remembers he swore, but did not realize this item was the one he swore about.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "With an oath, and it is hidden"
for forgetting the oath he is liable,
but he is not liable for forgetting the object.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with another detail from the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He brings a קרבן only for forgetting the oath, not for forgetting the object.

steps.title: What case counts as forced?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's first rule, that 'a man with an oath' leaves out someone forced, and asks what case that means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'A man with an oath' leaves out someone who was forced. What is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the first line of the ברייתא again so it can ask about it. It wants to know what kind of case counts as 'forced.' This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא never explained what 'forced' means for an oath. The גמרא is asking for a real example, and the answer will come next.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the ברייתא from step 20 again so it can ask about it.

phrases.english: "A man with an oath" leaves out someone who was forced.
What is the case?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: הָאָדָם בִּשְׁבוּעָה – פְּרָט לְאָנוּס. הֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the first rule of the ברייתא to ask for a clear case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A real example of an oath broken by someone who was forced.

steps.title: The story of רב כהנא and רב אסי swearing about what רב said
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers what an oath broken by אונס looks like. Two students each swore that רב had taught something different, and רב agreed with only one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like the case of רב כהנא and רב אסי. As they were getting up to leave רב, one said: 'I swear רב said it this way.' The other said: 'I swear רב said it this way.' When they came to רב, he said it the way one of them had said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 22 with a real story. Two students each swore to a different version of רב's words, so one of them swore to something untrue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both students were completely sure they were right when they swore. So the one who turned out wrong said something false, but not because he was careless or lying. The story sets up רב's ruling about that student in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath; here it means 'I swear!'

phrases.english: Like the case of Rav Kahana and Rav Asi,
when they were standing up to leave from before Rav,

phrases.aramaic: מָר אֲמַר: שְׁבוּעֲתָא דְּהָכִי אֲמַר רַב,
phrases.english: one said: I swear that Rav said it like this,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר אָמַר: שְׁבוּעֲתָא דְּהָכִי אֲמַר רַב.
phrases.english: and the other said: I swear that Rav said it like this.
phrases.notes: The words are the same, but each one meant a different version of what רב said.

phrases.english: When they came before Rav,
he said it like one of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22's question about what 'forced' (אונס) means for an oath.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is someone who swore to something he truly believed was true, and it turned out false.

steps.title: The other student asks whether he swore falsely
steps.stepSummary: The student whose version was wrong asks רב whether this means he swore a false oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: The other one said to רב: 'So did I swear falsely?!'
steps.whatsHappening: The student whose version was not accepted is upset. He asks רב whether he is now guilty of a false oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His words were false, so it looks like a שבועת שקר. The real question is whether a sincere mistake counts as a false oath. This prepares רב's answer in the next step.

phrases.english: The other one said to him:
And did I swear falsely?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אִידַּךְ: וַאֲנָא בְּשִׁיקְרָא אִישְׁתְּבַעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story by bringing out the problem: the student's oath turned out to be untrue.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an oath someone sincerely believed but that turned out wrong counts as a false oath.

steps.title: רב answers: your heart forced you
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that the student was forced by his own sincere belief, so this is אונס and not a false oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to him: 'Your heart forced you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב tells the student that his oath does not count as a lie. He truly believed it, so his own mind 'forced' him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the example of אונס that step 22 asked for. A person who swears to what he honestly thinks is true, and is wrong, is forced. That is why the ברייתא excludes him from bringing the קרבן.
steps.whatToRemember: An oath a person sincerely believed was true counts as אונס. Even if it turns out wrong, it is not a false oath, so there is no קרבן.

phrases.english: He said to him: Your heart forced you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the student's question and finishes the answer to step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A sincere mistake in an oath is אונס, not a false oath.

steps.title: The ברייתא: liable for forgetting the oath, not for forgetting the item
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back the next part of the ברייתא. The פסוק makes a person liable when he forgets the oath, not when he forgets the item.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And it is hidden from him' means the oath was hidden from him. You might think it also includes when the item was hidden from him. So the פסוק says, 'with an oath, and it is hidden from him.' He is liable for forgetting the oath, and not liable for forgetting the item.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא from step 21 and quotes it word for word. It is setting up a challenge against this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads 'with an oath' right next to 'it is hidden.' From that it learns that what must be forgotten is the oath itself. If someone remembered the oath but forgot which item it was about, he does not bring the קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is hidden from him (he forgot)
The item or object the oath is about

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new teaching. It is the same ברייתא from step 21, quoted again so the גמרא can challenge it.

phrases.english: "And it is hidden from him"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:4

phrases.english: means that the oath was hidden from him.
Might it also mean that the item was hidden from him?
The verse says: "With an oath, and it is hidden from him":
for forgetting the oath he is liable,
and he is not liable for forgetting the item.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the topic of אונס and goes back to the ברייתא's second rule from step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קרבן is brought only for forgetting the oath, not for forgetting the item.

steps.title: The West asks how you could forget the item but not the oath
steps.stepSummary: The scholars in ארץ ישראל agree you can forget an oath while remembering the item. But they ask what case there could be of forgetting the item without forgetting the oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West they laughed at this. Forgetting the oath without forgetting the item is easy to find. For example, he swore 'I will not eat wheat bread' but thinks he swore 'I will eat.' His oath is forgotten, but he remembers the item. But forgetting the item without forgetting the oath: what would that case be?
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars of ארץ ישראל make fun of the ברייתא's rule. They say the case it excludes (forgetting the item but remembering the oath) does not seem to exist. The next step tries to suggest such a case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forgetting the oath alone is easy to picture. He remembers 'wheat bread' but thinks his oath allowed it. The reverse seems impossible: if he remembers his oath, how could he not know which item it covers? If no such case exists, the ברייתא's exclusion seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense with... (sets up a contrast)
What is the case? What would it look like?

phrases.english: They laughed at it in the West:
phrases.notes: 'The West' means ארץ ישראל, which is west of בבל.

phrases.english: It makes sense with the oath:
you can find it without the item,
phrases.notes: He means forgetting the oath while still remembering the item.

phrases.english: for example, where he said:
"I swear that I will not eat wheat bread,"
and he thinks he said "that I will eat":
so his oath is forgotten,
but the item is remembered;
but forgetting the item without the oath,
what would that case be?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא's rule from step 26 by asking whether the case it excludes can even happen.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that there is no liability for forgetting the item (הֶעְלֵם חֵפֶץ).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a person remembers his oath, he seems to know which item it covers. So forgetting only the item looks impossible, and the ברייתא's exclusion seems to have no case.

steps.title: A suggested case: he forgot which bread he swore about
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a case of forgetting the item but not the oath. He swore off wheat bread but thinks he swore off barley bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, a man said, 'I swear I won't eat wheat bread,' but later thinks he said 'barley bread.' He remembers that he swore, but he forgot the item.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question from step 27 by offering a case where the person remembers his oath but forgets the item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man clearly knows he made an oath, so it seems his oath is 'remembered.' What he got wrong is which bread the oath was about, so it looks like a case of only forgetting the item.

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן דְּאָמַר: ״שְׁבוּעָה שֶׁלֹּא אוֹכַל פַּת חִטִּין״,
phrases.english: For example, where he said: 'On my oath, I will not eat wheat bread,'
and he thinks he said 'of barley'
so his oath he remembers,
but the item he forgot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a proposed answer to the question in step 27.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed there was no case of forgetting the item without forgetting the oath.
steps.terutzMaskana: Remembering that he swore while mixing up which bread fits that description.

steps.title: Forgetting what the oath covers is forgetting the oath
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. If he forgot which bread is forbidden, he has really forgotten his oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he forgot which item the oath was about, that is the same as forgetting the oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the case it just suggested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oath is its content. If he thinks he swore about barley, then the real oath about wheat is not in his mind at all. So this is just העלם שבועה, not a separate case of העלם חפץ.

phrases.english: Since the item is forgotten by him,
that is forgetting the oath!

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּחֶפְצָא אִינְּשִׁי לְהוּ, הַיְינוּ הֶעְלֵם שְׁבוּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case proposed in step 28.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Forgetting which item the oath covers is not separate from forgetting the oath itself.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: both kinds of forgetting are the same
steps.stepSummary: Since no case can be found, רבי אלעזר says forgetting the oath and forgetting the item are really one thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אלעזר said: this and that are one.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the suggested case failed, רבי אלעזר gives a new position: the ברייתא's split between forgetting the oath and forgetting the item does not really work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every case of forgetting the item turns out to be forgetting the oath too. So רבי אלעזר says they are one category, not two.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר: העלם שבועה and העלם חפץ are the same thing.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Elazar said:
This and that are one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the failed case in steps 28-29, gives a new approach.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no real difference between forgetting the oath and forgetting the item.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the bread-basket mix-up
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף argues there is a case of forgetting only the item. He reaches for barley bread, grabs wheat bread by mistake, and eats it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף challenged: Can you really not find forgetting the item without forgetting the oath? Here is a case. He swore off wheat bread, reached into the basket for barley bread, pulled out wheat bread, thought it was barley, and ate it. He remembered his oath. He just did not recognize the item.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges רבי אלעזר by giving a case where the person clearly remembers exactly what he swore and only mistakes the bread in his hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the man knows exactly that wheat bread is forbidden. His only mistake is about the physical bread in his hand. So it seems to be pure forgetting of the item, which would make it a separate category.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef challenges it:
Does this mean that the item without the oath
you cannot find?
phrases.notes: He means forgetting the item without forgetting the oath.

phrases.english: But you can find it:

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן דְּאָמַר ״שְׁבוּעָה שֶׁלֹּא אוֹכַל פַּת חִטִּין״,
phrases.english: for example, where he said: 'On my oath, I will not eat wheat bread,'
and he stretched his hand into the basket
to take barley bread;
and wheat bread came up in his hand,
and he thought it was barley and ate it;
his oath he remembers,
it is the item that he does not recognize!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אלעזר's claim in step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim that the two kinds of forgetting are one
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A counterexample where the oath is fully remembered and only the physical item is mistaken.

steps.title: אביי: what matters is the bread he ate
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the קרבן is only for the bread he actually ate. About that bread, he did not know his oath forbade it, so it is העלם שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Do you make him bring a קרבן for anything other than what he holds in his hand? For that bread, it is forgetting the oath!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רבי אלעזר and shows that רב יוסף's case is also really forgetting the oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sin is eating this specific bread. At that moment he did not know that his oath applied to this bread. So about the act that makes him liable, he was unaware of the oath, and רבי אלעזר is right that they are one.

keyTerms.meaning: do you at all (opening a rhetorical question)
that he holds in his hand

steps.whatToRemember: Forgetting is judged by the actual act. When he ate the bread, he did not know the oath covered it, so it counts as העלם שבועה.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Do you make him liable for an offering at all
except for what he holds in his hand?
That is forgetting the oath!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge from step 31.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In the basket case he remembers the oath and only mistakes the item.
steps.terutzMaskana: Liability is for the bread in his hand, and about that bread he was unaware of the oath.

steps.title: Another version: אביי challenges רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: In a second version of the exchange, אביי objects to רב יוסף. Whatever the man was thinking, the קרבן is brought for the bread he actually ate, and about that bread he forgot the oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: אביי said to רב יוסף: In the end, the קרבן he brings is for this bread, and about this bread he forgot the oath!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא retells the exchange from Steps 31–32 a second way. Here אביי's words are a challenge to רב יוסף, and the next step gives רב יוסף's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי looks only at the wheat bread that was eaten. The man did not realize his oath forbade that bread, so this is העלם שבועה. That would mean רב יוסף has still not found a clean case of forgetting only the item.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version: a second way the same discussion was passed down
An offering, here the sin-offering for breaking an oath by mistake
Forgetting the oath, meaning not knowing that one's oath forbids this

phrases.english: Another version:
Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
In the end, the offering that he brings
for this bread, at any rate,
is for forgetting the oath!

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא – אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב יוֹסֵף: סוֹף סוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a second version of Step 32. אביי's same point is now presented as a challenge that רב יוסף will answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's case of grabbing wheat bread instead of barley bread
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The קרבן is for the bread that was eaten. About that bread he did not know the oath forbade it, so it is still העלם שבועה.

steps.title: רב יוסף: if knowing it is wheat would stop him, he forgot the item
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף defends his case. Once the man realizes the bread is wheat, he stops eating it. So what he was missing was knowledge of the item, not of the oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף would say to you: Since he holds back from it as soon as he knows it is wheat, this is העלם חפץ.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי's challenge and keeps his case standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף judges the case by what would have stopped the man. He remembered his oath against wheat perfectly well. The only thing he was missing was that this bread was wheat, so his mistake was about the item.

keyTerms.meaning: Forgetting the item, meaning not knowing what the object in front of you is
He holds back from it, he stops

steps.confusionAlert: אביי and רב יוסף agree on the facts. They disagree only on how to describe his mistake: as not knowing the oath covers this bread, or as not knowing what this bread is.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef would say to you:
Since when he knows about it
that it is wheat, he holds back from it,
it is forgetting the item.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in Step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what kind of mistake it was
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since he did not know the oath forbade this bread, it is העלם שבועה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the only thing that would stop him is knowing it is wheat, his mistake is העלם חפץ.

steps.title: רבא asks: what if he forgot both?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן what the law is when a person forgot both the oath and the item.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן: If he forgot both this and that, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. It is no longer about finding a case of one kind of forgetting. It asks what to do when both kinds of forgetting happen together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forgetting the oath leads to a קרבן, while forgetting the item does not. When both happen at once, it is unclear which one decides the case.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him, a formal question put to a teacher
This and that, meaning both the oath and the item

phrases.english: Rava asked of Rav Naḥman:
If he has forgetting of both this and that, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining each kind of forgetting to a case where both happen together.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a person who forgot both the oath and the item liable to a קרבן or exempt?

steps.title: רב נחמן: he forgot the oath, so he is liable
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that since he did forget the oath, he is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He has forgotten the oath, so he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב נחמן, forgetting the oath is enough to make him liable. The fact that he also forgot the item does not remove that.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally, in his hand: it is present in his case
Liable, here meaning he must bring a קרבן

phrases.english: He said to him:
Look, he has forgetting of the oath, and he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הֲרֵי הֶעְלֵם שְׁבוּעָה בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question from Step 35.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Liable, because forgetting the oath is present.

steps.title: רבא: on the contrary, he forgot the item, so he is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבא turns the argument around. He also forgot the item, so he should be exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, he has forgotten the item, so he is exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רב נחמן with the opposite argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is the same but points the other way. If one kind of forgetting is present, so is the other, and forgetting the item leads to exemption. Nothing yet shows which kind should decide.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary, the opposite is true

phrases.english: On the contrary,
look, he has forgetting of the item, and he is exempt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's answer in Step 36 by flipping it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that he is liable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Forgetting the item is just as present as forgetting the oath, and it leads to exemption, so why should liability win?

steps.title: רב אשי: check what makes him stop
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a practical test. If being reminded of the oath would stop him, he is liable. If being reminded of the item would stop him, he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: We look. If the oath is what makes him hold back, he has forgotten the oath and is liable. If the item is what makes him hold back, he has forgotten the item and is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי proposes a way to settle the argument between רב נחמן and רבא. The next steps reject this test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of asking which kind of forgetting is present, רב אשי asks which reminder actually makes the person stop. That decides which kind of forgetting really caused the sin. This uses the same idea as רב יוסף's reasoning in Step 34.

keyTerms.meaning: We look, we check the facts

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי suggests judging by which reminder would make him stop. רבינא rejects this test in step 39, and step 40 concludes there is no difference.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the test that רבינא attacks in the next step, which leads to the conclusion 'אלא לא שנא'.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: We look:
if he holds back because of the oath,
then he has forgetting of the oath, and he is liable;
if he holds back because of the item,
then he has forgetting of the item, and he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the disagreement between רב נחמן (Step 36) and רבא (Step 37).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב אשי's proposal: judge by which reminder would make him stop. This is rejected in steps 39-40.

steps.title: רבינא challenges the reminder test
steps.stepSummary: רבינא argues that רב אשי's test fails, because the oath and the item always work together to stop the person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Does he hold back from breaking the oath for any reason other than the item? And does he hold back from the item for any reason other than the oath?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks רב אשי's practical test from step 38. He says the two kinds of reminders cannot really be separated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי said: if reminding him of the oath would stop him, he is liable, and if reminding him of the item would stop him, he is exempt. רבינא points out that a reminder of the oath only stops him because he connects it to this item. A reminder of the item only stops him because he connects it to the oath. So whichever reminder stops him, he needed both pieces together, and the test tells us nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it anything other than... (a way of saying 'it is only because of')
The item or object the oath is about

steps.confusionAlert: The two questions are not real questions. They are a challenge, and both of them mean the same thing: the oath and the item depend on each other.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
Does he hold back from the oath
for any reason other than the item?!
Does he hold back from the item
for any reason other than the oath?!

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלוּם פָּרֵישׁ מִשְּׁבוּעָה אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם חֵפֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the practical test רב אשי gave in step 38.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's test: a reminder of the oath means liable, a reminder of the item means exempt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each reminder only works because of the other one, so which reminder stopped him does not show which piece of knowledge he was missing.

steps.title: There is no difference between the two
steps.stepSummary: Because the test fails, the גמרא concludes that the two ways of being reminded are the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: After רבינא's challenge, the גמרא concludes that we cannot split the cases by which reminder would stop him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's split between 'reminded of the oath' and 'reminded of the item' is dropped. The words 'אלא לא שנא' mean that both cases get the same ruling. רש״י explains that the result is פטור, just as he explained in the same case with טומאה and the מקדש (שבועות יט.).
steps.whatToRemember: For someone who forgot both the oath and the item, we do not judge him by which reminder would stop him. רבינא shows the two are bound together, so there is no difference between the cases.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ends the discussion of forgetting both the oath and the item, and it removes רב אשי's practical test.

phrases.english: Rather, there is no difference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from רבינא's challenge in step 39.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The reminder test does not separate the cases. Both are treated the same, and רש״י says he is פטור.

steps.title: רבא opens a new question to רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces another question that רבא asked רב נחמן. The question itself comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is getting ready for a new question from רבא to רב נחמן, and the question itself comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the topic of forgetting both the oath and the item is closed, רבא brings a new question to רב נחמן. The question is not stated yet, so this line only opens it.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a question about the law)

phrases.english: Rava asked of Rav Nachman:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question after the previous discussion ended.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Not stated yet. The question itself comes next in the text.
